rows: Right. The job is simple: do the technique properly and get everybody home.
Brawling is fine, as long as nobody gets hurt for the sake of it.
Risk is a shift that goes wrong. I have seen it. Do not make me see it again.
Slow is fine, as long as it is safe. I have never once regretted taking my time.
The people paid, so we give them a decent shift. That is all.
Short answer: I do the job properly, every time.
I have done this long enough to know what the job needs. I am still doing it.
Check the stance is safe. Nothing clever, just reliable.
You bang on about technique. Show it safely. Show me one hold you can do without hurting the other person.
Strikes are fine in the right place. Not the wrong one.
A risk is a shift you cannot finish. Think about who has to clean up after you.
Stalling is a shirker's trick. Not what I do.
The people want a decent contest. Give them one and make it safe.
Among the best, you say. Show me the work. I will believe it when I see you turn up every day.
You are proud of your {strength}. Right, on you go. Be proud of the work, not the noise.
I have clocked your {strength}. It is fine, but it could be tidier.
You kept it steady, fair play. Right, on you go. That is how you stay out of trouble.
Agreed, for the moment. We agree on the basics, which is more than I expected.
I could go on about that. I would rather save my breath for the mat.
One fall, and everybody gets home. Keep me down, and I will shake your hand after.
On the mat, we go slowly and check each other. Simple.
Grounded or standing, you do not do anything daft. Got it?
Keep your eyes where they should be. I want to see you do it properly.
Decent answer, that. That is how the job is done.
You have not replied. Take your time. Take your time, but answer.
Agreed, for the moment. We will keep it straight.
Fair point, that. I will take it. We will sort the rest out at the bell.
I will do this match properly, and I will look after you while I do it.
My approach is steady and safe. Nothing clever.
Whatever happens, we both get out of there in one piece.
Not done yet, mind. There is still a job to do.
I have one thing left to say, and it is about looking after each other.
